public.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
public.description: Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the root comes first, then the left and right children of each non-null node in queue order; null means absent and trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no root. Node values are unique; target names an existing node. Return the values of nodes exactly k edges from target, sorted numerically ascending. There are 1 to 500 nodes with values from -10000 to 10000, and k is 0 to 500.
hints: Add parent edges to turn the tree into an undirected graph.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026. Uses a standard algorithmic pattern; no third-party exercise text used.

javascript.signature: allNodesDistanceKInBinaryTree(values: (number|null)[], target: number, k: number): number[]

typescript.signature: allNodesDistanceKInBinaryTree(values: (number|null)[], target: number, k: number): number[]

explanation: Breadth-first expansion from target reaches exactly the requested distance. Sort the last frontier. O(n plus output sorting) time and O(n) space.
